answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Wrapped-asset age proof across a bridge. It demands an asset that crossed a bridge two years ago, and the nectar is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that an asset that crossed a bridge two years ago — so privacy survives, and the terrace is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The pigment is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
